title: Frosted Pumpkin Bars

items: 1 can (15 oz) pumpkin purée (not pumpkin pie filling)
2 cups all-purpose flour, spooned and leveled
¼ cup (½ stick) unsalted butter, softened

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Coat the 10×15-inch pan well with nonstick spray.
In a large bowl, whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil and sugar until smooth.

In a second bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt. Add it to the pumpkin mixture and stir with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. Overmixing makes the bars tough.
Spread the batter evenly into the pan, pushing it into the corners. Bake 25–30 min, until the center springs back when pressed lightly and a toothpick comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, at least 1½ hr. Frosting melts on warm bars.

Make the frosting: beat the cream cheese and butter with a hand mixer on medium 1–2 min, until smooth. Add the powdered sugar 1 cup at a time on low, then the vanilla, and beat on medium 1 min, until fluffy.
Spread the frosting over the cooled bars. Warm the caramel in the microwave 10–15 seconds, until pourable, and drizzle it over the top in thin lines with a spoon.
Chill 30 min to set, then cut into 24 squares (4 rows by 6).
tips: For a warmer spice flavor, swap the cinnamon for 1 Tbsp pumpkin pie spice.
Make ahead: bake and frost the day before, cover and refrigerate. Add the caramel just before serving so the lines stay neat.
A 9×13-inch pan works too. The bars are thicker, so bake 30–35 min.
storage: Fridge, covered, up to 5 days; the cream cheese frosting must stay cold. Freeze frosted bars without the caramel up to 3 months and thaw overnight in the fridge. Serve cold or after 15 min at room temperature.
